items.note: Bes lies in the fork between the Betwa and the Bes; generally identified with ancient Wessanagara (Vaishyanagari) or Vidisha.
Buddhist literature: Prince Ashoka halted here and married Devi, a local banker's daughter; the city was a centre of business and wealth, donors from Wessanagara named in Sanchi records.
Bhilsa said to have been founded and flourished at the cost of the old city of Besnagar, taking its square stones for its outer walls.
Cunningham made a complete survey of the ruined city in 1874-75 to 1876-77.
refs: Cunningham, Archaeological Survey of India Reports (1874-75 to 1876-77)

items.note: Heliodorus pillar inscription: Garuda-dhvaja erected by Heliodora son of Diya, a Bhagavata of Takshasila, envoy of Antalikita to the local prince Bhagabhadra.
Railing pieces found by Cunningham inscribed with donor records in Ashokan characters; coping-stone shows a procession with relic-caskets.
Latest date for the Indo-Bactrian king is 140 B.C.; the pillar proves an early temple of Vasudeva, whose fame inspired a Greek ambassador.
Garudadwaja of Vindhyan quartzitic sandstone, pinkish brown, rough surface, shaft and capital each a monolith.
Second Garuda standard: Bhagavata son of Gotami set it up at the best temple of Vasudeva in the twelfth year of Maharaja Bhagavata.
Garuda image ascribed to age of Chandragupta II, 5th century, probably crowning the Kham Baba pillar.
Kham Baba pillar worshipped as a deified column by Bhois or Dhimars, with a Shaiva priest holding the inam from Gwalior Darbar.
Railings assigned to 165 B.C. and 140 B.C.; Babaji's mound possibly the site of the Vasudeva temple.
Temple possibly pilfered to build Bhilsa town, which came into existence about the 8th century A.D.
Mauryan or pre-Mauryan canal: river Bes dammed and water carried to irrigate fields through a network of canals.
Excavation on the eastern bank where ancient Vidisha stood yielded three sacrificial kundas, square, oblong and Yoni type.
Coins of Ishvaradatta and Naga kings fix the kundas to the beginning of the 4th century A.D.
Clay seals with sacrificial terms hota, pota, mamantra; donor Timitra taken as a Sanskritised Greek Demetrius.
Stratum of Maurya habitation; only Maurya structures were four or five wells of burnt earthenware rings.
1963-64 and 1964-65 cutting at the Bes-Betwa confluence revealed six periods of habitation, from before NBP ware to post-Gupta times.
Huge temple remains in the Kham Baba area; ASI exploration around Vidisha found a sequence from the Chalcolithic to the early Mediaeval period.
Fortification wall of ancient Besnagar built probably in the 2nd century B.C. as a huge palace wall per ancient city planning.
Criss-cross rubble construction of thin walls and cross walls packed with rubble, making the wall cheaper and stronger.
A pilgrims record on a pillar of the Athakhamba at Gyaraspur is dated Vikrama Samvat 1039, A.D. 982.

items.note: Neelakantheshwara temple near Lateri, 10th century, with broken images resembling those at the Neelakantheshwara temple of Udaipur, ancient Udayapura in Basoda Tahsil.
Kurwai on the Betwa: its fort and most houses are built of the gneiss rock abundant in the neighbourhood, roofed with big slabs.
Old town of Badoh said to have been destroyed by the Muhammadans, possibly by Alamgir or Aurangzeb.
Inscribed slab in a baori at Pathari records its construction by Maharaja Prithviraj Ju Deva, dated 1676, mentioning Aurangzeb's reign.
Shamshabad (Basoda Tahsil): palace and mosque built early 17th century by Shams Khan; Persian inscription dated 1641 A.D.
